name: Biomechanics: Myolark
subtitle: Biomechanics Labs and Quizzes
shortDescription: Learn how bodies move and load by building: joint forces, gait, muscle models, bone and flow benches. 25 cited labs and adaptive quizzes. Free with ads.
longDescription:
Biomechanics: Myolark is a course in the mechanics of the human body, from the force in an elbow holding a grocery bag to the pressure wave in an artery. It is written for engineering, kinesiology and movement-science students who want to calculate, not just memorise.

Two ways in. The classical view follows 11 units and 62 topics: statics of the body, kinematics and gait, anthropometry and inverse dynamics, tissue mechanics, muscle, musculoskeletal modelling, fluids and impact, 3D segment orientation and signals, sport and ergonomics, joints and assistive devices, and computational extensions. The real-world view starts from something to make, such as a one-leg balance rig, a phone-video knee tracker, a force-plate jump lab or a bone-implant bar, and brings in each lesson when the build needs it. 23 builds and the course share one progress record, so you can change view without losing anything.

25 labs run on the graphics chip and respond as you drag. Rotate a 3D elbow or hip, watch a Hill muscle curve move, bend a long bone and see stress colours, stretch a tendon, send a pulse wave down a vessel, compose rotations or spherical quaternion interpolation, and test a spring-mass hopper or a lifting task. Every lab names its formula, cites its source and shows an independent second computation.

Practice adapts as you go. 496 original questions span four levels from Beginner to Research; 248 are numeric and each was solved by two methods before it was written in, and 248 are conceptual items kept for practice. The app tracks what you know, brings back what is fading and points to the lesson behind each slip, always gently. Pick 5, 10, 20 or 40 questions or a length you choose. 13 case studies and 3 timed mock papers are included, with no ads during mocks.

Coverage in exact numbers: 52 of 62 topics have a direct heading match in an opened source, 6 match loosely and 4 rest on printed references that could not be opened online; the Coverage screen lists each. Segment fractions and tissue constants are rounded teaching values.

Citations open in a wide sheet with Back and Close. Text size can be set from 50 to 300 percent. No account, no network needed, and your progress stays on your device.

Free with ads at natural breaks. A short video unlocks Plus features for a day, or an optional monthly subscription removes ads and unlocks everything. Lessons, worked solutions and progress are never locked. The subscription renews monthly until you cancel it in your account settings, and the store shows the price before you confirm. Restore purchases is in More.

Education only. This is not medical, rehabilitation, injury or workplace-safety advice. No affiliation with any university, standards body or publisher named in the sources.
